column3: But Saul, still breathing threats and murder against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest
and asked him for letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any who belonged to the Way, both men and women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.
Now as he was traveling and drawing near Damascus, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.
And falling to the ground, he heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?”
He said, “Who are you, Lord?” And he said, “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
But get up and enter the city, and it will be told you what you must do.”
Now the men traveling with him stood speechless, hearing the voice but seeing no one.
Saul got up from the ground, but though his eyes were open, he could see nothing. So leading him by the hand, they brought him into Damascus.
And for three days he was unable to see, and he neither ate nor drank.
Now there was a certain disciple in Damascus named Ananias, and the Lord said to him in a vision, “Ananias!” He said, “Look, I am here, Lord.”
The Lord said to him, “Get up, go to the street called Straight, and in the house of Judas look for a man from Tarsus named Saul. For look, he is praying,
and he has seen in a vision a man named Ananias coming in and laying hands on him so that he may see again.”
But Ananias answered, “Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how many evil things he has done to your holy ones in Jerusalem.
And here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on your name.”
But the Lord said to him, “Go, because this man is a chosen instrument to me, to carry my name before Gentiles and kings and sons of Israel.
For I will show him how much he must suffer for my name.”

So Ananias went and entered the house. Laying his hands on him, he said, “Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road by which you came, has sent me so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
And immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he saw again. Then he got up and was baptized,
and after taking food, he was strengthened. And he was with the disciples in Damascus for some days.
And immediately he began proclaiming Jesus in the synagogues, that this one is the Son of God.

All who heard him were astonished and saying, “Is this not the one who devastated in Jerusalem those calling on this name, and came here for this purpose, to bring them bound before the chief priests?”
But Saul was becoming even stronger and was confounding the Jews living in Damascus, proving that this one is the Christ.
Now when many days had been completed, the Jews plotted together to kill him,
but their plot became known to Saul. And they were watching the gates both day and night so that they might kill him.
But his disciples took him by night and lowered him through the wall, letting him down in a basket.
When he arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.

But Barnabas took him, brought him to the apostles, and described to them how on the road he had seen the Lord, and that he had spoken to him, and how in Damascus he had spoken boldly in the name of Jesus.
And he was with them, going in and out in Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.
He was speaking and disputing with the Hellenists, but they were trying to kill him.
When the brothers learned this, they brought him down to Caesarea and sent him away to Tarsus.
So the assembly throughout all Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace, being built up and walking in the fear of the Lord and in the encouragement of the Holy Spirit, and it was multiplying.
Now as Peter was traveling through all the regions, he also came down to the holy ones living in Lydda.
There he found a certain man named Aeneas, who had been lying on a mat for eight years, being paralyzed.
Peter said to him, “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed for yourself.” And immediately he got up.
And all who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.
Now in Joppa there was a certain disciple named Tabitha, which translated is called Dorcas. She was full of good works and acts of mercy that she was doing.
And in those days she became sick and died. After washing her, they laid her in an upstairs room.
Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, urging, “Do not delay in coming to us.”

So Peter got up and went with them. When he arrived, they brought him up to the upstairs room, and all the widows stood beside him, weeping and showing tunics and garments that Dorcas had made while she was with them.
But Peter put them all outside, knelt down, and prayed. Turning to the body, he said, “Tabitha, get up!” And she opened her eyes, and seeing Peter, she sat up.
And giving her his hand, he raised her up. Then calling the holy ones and the widows, he presented her alive.
And it became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.
And it happened that he stayed many days in Joppa with a certain Simon, a tanner.
